name: OR-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Salinas is an incumbent in a district with a 6-point Democratic lean
David Russ has raised only about $13,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 96%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Salinas: a Democratic-leaning seat, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a challenger who has raised almost nothing. Markets price her near certain, and nothing in the evidence suggests moving off the baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Salinas or a strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Andrea Salinas, the Democratic incumbent, is running for a second full term in a district that leans Democratic by about six points. She has raised over $1.6 million and holds more than $600,000 on hand, while Republican David Russ has raised under $13,000 and has almost no cash. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets give her roughly a 96 percent chance of winning.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, which all point the same way: incumbency, a favorable partisan lean, and a decisive financial advantage. The forecast places Salinas well ahead, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling in a relatively new district.
